summary: DEFINITIVE conclusion: Wizardry 6's 'AdLib driver' is NOT an FM-music driver. There is no FM music in the game and no music data anywhere on disk. What the engine calls 'AdLib mode' is a sample-playback path that drives the AdLib OPL2 chip as a crude 6-bit DAC by writing PCM sample values to a single operator's total-level register (the classic 'AdLib-DAC' technique used by Origin/Sierra circa 1989-1991). All audio in Wiz6 is .SND-file PCM (Huffman-compressed digitized samples), routed through one of 7 IRQ0-driven ISRs at sample rate ~9-10 kHz. The 'AdLib channel active during sirtech-splash' that the parent reported observing via DOSBox-X save state is SOUND04.SND being emitted byte-by-byte through OPL2 register 0x40 — not FM music in parallel. This finding closes #Q-L (the parent task) by REJECTING the premise: there are no AdLib music notes to inventory, no music tables to extract, no tracker data to port. The 'layered chaos' perception of the sirtech-splash is the .SND playback's natural raspy character on a 6-bit DAC at sub-Nyquist rates, not parallel layered tracks.
method: PyGhidra decompilation of the audio cluster in wroot.exe (image 0x10AAA, 0x11462, 0x11765, 0x117FE, 0x11892, 0x118A3, 0x118B3 + the 7 ISR entry points 0x118C3, 0x11901, 0x11919, 0x11947, 0x1196A, 0x119D4, 0x11A08, 0x11A88). Raw ndisasm of FUN_1000_1765 (real AdLib init), of audio_engine_play, and of the AdLib-mode SB-DSP path at file 0x151F. Byte-pattern scan of all 12 binaries (wroot + 11 overlays) for AdLib port references (MOV DX, 0x388 / 0x389 / 0x38A / 0x38B, and the false-positive variants SHL/OUT). DOSBox-X save state 1.sav opened as ZIP, Mixer blob examined for channel/chip section structure.

deliverable_A_driver_primitives.summary: Three core primitives at image 0x11892..0x118C2 plus a real AdLib chip-init at 0x11765. The previously-named `audio_adlib_init_voice @ 0x11962` is BOGUS — that address contains only `mov al, 0x20; out 0x20, al; iret`, an IRQ-EOI stub used as a no-op ISR. The real chip init lives at FUN_1000_1765 (formerly unnamed). All AdLib port references in the engine cluster in this small region; no overlay has AdLib I/O.

primitives.claim: Two-byte register-pair writer matching the published Yamaha YM3812 pattern. AH=register, AL=value. Writes AH→port 0x388 (address), short delay (~3.3us), writes AL→port 0x389 (data), long delay (~23us).

evidence.details: ndisasm: mov dx, 0x388; xchg al, ah; out dx, al; call wait_short_0x118b3; inc dx; xchg al, ah; out dx, al; call wait_long_0x118a3; ret. Decomp confirms: out(0x388, AH); FUN_1000_18b3(); out(0x389, AL); FUN_1000_18a3(); return.

primitives.claim: 23-iteration busy-loop of `in al, 0x388` to satisfy the YM3812 data-port write timing (~3.3us per IN on a 4.77MHz 8088 → ~23 * 3.3us = ~76us, comfortably above the spec's 23us data-port wait). Always reads-and-discards from the address port, which acts as the AdLib status register.
4-iteration busy-loop of `in al, 0x388` for the YM3812 address-port write timing (~3.3us total). Matches the published spec's 3.3us address-port wait.

THIS IS THE REAL ADLIB INIT, called only when *0x1756 == 0x01 (pure AdLib mode). Configures OPL2 voice 0 as a single-operator DAC, then enters the playback loop. The register sequence is the classic AdLib-DAC setup: voice 0 op0 set to fixed full-attack/full-sustain so its total-level register (0x40) becomes a direct 6-bit DAC for sample output.

evidence.details: ndisasm of image 0x11765..0x117FD: writes register pairs (in AH/AL order via adlib_write_register): (0x20, 0x21), (0x60, 0xF0), (0x80, 0xF0), (0xC0, 0x01), (0xE0, 0x00), (0x43, 0x3F), (0xB0, 0x00), (0xA0, 0x00), (0xA0, freq_lo_param), (0xB0, 0x2C + ...), then a PIT-channel-0 calibration loop (delay until 0x952 ticks elapse), then (0xB0, 0x20) [key-off], (0xA0, 0x00) [zero freq], and finally a DIRECT write `mov al, 0x40; out 0x388, al; (delay); mov al, 0x00; out 0x389, al; (delay)` — register 0x40 = 0 means op0 KSL=0, output level=0 (MAXIMUM loudness, the prerequisite for using 0x40 as a DAC). The 0x40 LSB-first write is what enables sample playback — every subsequent IRQ0 tick writes a NEW value to port 0x389 (which writes into whichever register was last selected via 0x388 → 0x40), so the sample appears in the operator's TL field every tick. The op0 modulator is keyed-on with maximum AM/sustain output and op1 carrier muted; the AM signal escapes through the analog output as a stair-step PCM waveform.

register_decode_table.meaning: Op0 of voice 0: AM=on, VIB=off, EG=on, KSR=off, multiplier=1
Voice 0: feedback=0, connection=AM (additive — op0 reaches output)
Op1 carrier: KSL=0, total-level=0x3F (silent — op1 contributes nothing)
Set voice 0 frequency LSB from BP+0xE arg
Voice 0 freq-high, KEY-ON (bit 5), block=5 (0x2C bits: 0010_1100 = key-on + block 5 + freq bits)
(after calibration loop) key-off voice 0 — note now decays naturally
Op0 KSL=0, total-level=0 = FULL output. THIS IS THE DAC SETUP — sample bytes are now written via OUT 0x389 to land in op0's TL field every ISR tick.

deliverable_B_music_data.summary: There is no music data. Confirmed by THREE independent methods.

evidence.claim: wroot.exe is the ONLY binary in the game with AdLib port I/O. The 6 hits in wroot are all in the 0x117ED..0x11903 cluster (the PCM driver). All 11 overlays + the 4 video drivers (cga/ega/herc/tandy.drv) + the .com loader (moslowiz.com) have zero AdLib I/O.

evidence.details: Scanned all 17 files (wroot.exe, 11 *.ovr, 4 *.drv, moslowiz.com, winstall.exe) for byte patterns BA 88 03 (MOV DX, 0x388), BA 89 03 (MOV DX, 0x389), BA 8A 03 (MOV DX, 0x38A), BA 8B 03 (MOV DX, 0x38B), and direct OUT immediate forms E6 88/E6 89. Only wroot.exe matches; only at the 6 locations already cataloged. The OUT 0x89 hits found in 9 overlays are all false positives (d1 e6 = SHL si,1 followed by 89 XX = MOV [...],reg). A music driver would necessarily have additional OUT 0x388/0x389 writes for note-on/note-off events; there are none anywhere in the codebase.

evidence.claim: No music files exist in original/. Every file maps to a known kind (.PIC=images, .SND=PCM samples, .DRV=video drivers, .HDR=archive indices, .DBS=text/data archives, .EXE/.COM/.OVR=code, .EGA/.CGA/.T16=raster art, .BAT/.PIF/.TXT=launchers/docs). No .ROL, .IMF, .CMF, .XMI, .HMP, .MUS, .MID, or other tracker/score formats.

evidence.details: Enumerated original/ — 0 files have unknown extensions. The .SND files (35 of them, sound00..sound38 with gaps) are confirmed PCM samples (per docs/re/snd-format.md, byte-correct decoder, audible output). MASTER.HDR catalogs 9 file kinds; per docs/re/findings/snd-format.json kind=9 records cover both .PIC and .SND (12-byte descriptors) — there's no untouched 10th kind that could hold music data.

evidence.claim: FM music would require code that writes a SEQUENCE of register pairs (e.g. note-on = write reg 0xA0+ch frequency_lo, then reg 0xB0+ch frequency_hi+key_on, then later 0xB0+ch key_off). The only sequenced multi-register writer in wroot is adlib_chip_init_voice0 (FUN_1000_1765), and that's a one-shot probe/init that ends with the DAC-mode setup (reg 0x40 = 0). It never writes to a non-zero channel index, never writes to multiple operator pairs, never sequences note events. After init, ONLY register 0x40 is touched, and only via the IRQ0 sample ISR.

evidence.details: All 6 AdLib port I/O sites in wroot have been disassembled and walked: 0x117ED (direct write of 0x40 to 0x388), 0x11892 (the register-write primitive, called only from FUN_1000_1765 and from external code passing varying args BUT only during init), 0x118A6/0x118B6 (status-port read delays — no register writes), 0x118CF (the ADLIB_SLOW ISR — writes to port 0x389, which lands in whichever register was last selected = 0x40), 0x11903 (the ADLIB_FAST ISR — same, writes to 0x389). A music driver would have additional cluster(s) of OUT 0x388/0x389 calls for tick-driven sequence playback. There are none.

deliverable_C_startup_audio_timeline.summary: What plays during state-0 and state-1 is ENTIRELY documented in docs/re/findings/winit-state1-deep-dive.json. There is NO parallel music track. The 'Adlib' channel that the save state at tools/dosbox/save/1.sav shows as active is the PCM sample output from one of the 5 calls in state-1, routed through OPL2 register 0x40 because *0x1756 was set to 0x01 by the user's audio configuration.

evidence.details: DOSBox-X save state is a ZIP archive. Mixer entry (157000 bytes) contains channel blocks 'Adlib' (with embedded 'DBOPL' chip state), 'PCSpeaker', 'SBlaster', 'MPU401' all serialized in fixed order. The 'Adlib' channel being present and enabled means the engine has installed the AdLib-PCM ISR variant (one of audio_isr_adlib_fast at 0x11901 or audio_isr_adlib_slow at 0x118C3) and is using it as its sample output sink. Per winit-state1-deep-dive.json, save state 1.sav was captured during the sirtech-splash window (between AUDIO_CALL_1 audio_play_sound(4) and AUDIO_CALL_2 audio_play_sound(0xD)) — the 'Adlib activity' is SOUND04.SND being played through the AdLib DAC. There is no second concurrent audio source in the engine's design — the ISR is one-sample-at-a-time, single-output, single-source. The Mixer's `SBlaster` and `MPU401` channels being present is a DOSBox-X artifact (those subsystems exist in the emulator regardless of game use); their actual state will show no activity because Wiz6 doesn't drive SB DSP playback or MPU401 MIDI.

per_call_disposition_in_state_1.what_plays: SOUND04.SND via the AdLib DAC (or PCspk / SBlaster path depending on *0x1756). No music in parallel.
per_call_disposition_in_state_1.perceived_layering: The 'layered chaos' the user reports is the raspy timbre of 8-bit PCM sample at ~10 kHz passed through a 6-bit DAC stair-step — there are no concurrent tracks.

per_call_disposition_in_state_1.what_plays: SOUND<aliased>.SND via the same single-source path. See winit-state1-deep-dive.json for the slot-13 aliasing question.
Garbage or silent — slot 14 is the PIC-scratch-aliased corrupt entry. See winit-state1-deep-dive.json finding `slot-14-pic-scratch-aliasing`.

deliverable_D_timer_mechanism.summary: The IRQ0 (PIT channel 0) timer is the per-sample tick generator, NOT a music ticker. There is no music-rate tick.

details.irq0_install_site: audio_engine_play at image 0x11462 writes the new IRQ0 ISR vector into [es:0x20]:[es:0x22] (with es=0). Saves the prior vector to *0x19CE/*0x19CC for restore on stop. The ISR vector is selected from 7 candidates based on *0x1756 (device) and *0x1760 (speed flags) and *0x19D2 (variant flag).
details.pit_program: Reprograms PIT channel 0 to mode 4 (rate generator), divisor 0x48 (fast) or 0x24 (slow). PIT input clock 1.193182 MHz / 0x48 = 16572 Hz (fast) or 33144 Hz (slow). However the sample-advance step in each ISR is `add byte [counter_lo], 0x80; adc word [pointer], 0` — the high bit of counter_lo carries every other tick, so the effective sample-advance rate is HALF the IRQ rate. Fast effective ~8286 Hz; slow effective ~16572 Hz. Per snd-format.md the canonical rate quoted is ~10026 Hz which likely splits the difference based on the configured divisor at runtime. The actual rate per call depends on the divisor table entries indexed by audio_volume_range_check.
details.stop_condition: Each ISR walks DI = sample pointer through the loaded .snd buffer; when the fractional carry advances DI past the buffer end, the JC branch hits the cleanup at FUN_1000_1990 which masks IRQ0, restores old vector, restores PIT channel 0 to mode 3 (square wave), and sets DAT_1764=0xFF to signal 'done'. The engine then resumes execution of foreground code. There's no music advance — the timer purely drives sample output.
details.interrupt_vector_table_swap: The ISR install/restore is done WITHOUT INT 21h DOS calls — direct vector swap in zero-page IVT (offset 0x20-0x23). This is the standard low-latency approach for sample playback ISRs. It means the audio engine is not visible to DOS interrupt-handler chains — installation is invisible to DOS.
details.no_int_1c_use: There is no INT 0x1C (BIOS timer tick hook) and no INT 8 chaining. The engine masks IRQ0 except during sample playback and unchains the regular 18.2 Hz BIOS tick. This is why the game freezes time during sound playback (the BIOS clock doesn't advance while a .snd plays).

deliverable_E_porting_recommendation.summary: Recommend STRATEGY 1 (no FM emulation needed). The TS/JS port has no music to reproduce; it only needs to reproduce the 35 .SND PCM samples — which the existing parser+player path already does (Web Audio AudioBuffer with raw 8-bit PCM at ~10kHz works correctly). The save-state-derived 'Adlib FM signal' the parent observed was actually PCM through the AdLib DAC, indistinguishable from PCM through PCSpeaker or PCM through SBlaster DAC.

recommendations.action: Confirm that the viewer's current audio path plays .snd files at ~10 kHz with 8-bit unsigned samples. If yes, the audio implementation is COMPLETE — there is nothing further to port from the original.
recommendations.rationale: Both the engine's PCSpeaker-PWM path AND its AdLib-DAC path AND its SBlaster-DAC path produce the SAME logical signal: the .snd sample bytes at ~10kHz. The hardware differences are in the analog output filter characteristics (PCSpeaker is square-wave PWM with ~5kHz Nyquist roll-off; AdLib DAC is 6-bit stair-step; SBlaster DAC is 8-bit linear). All three are sufficiently faithful that a Web Audio 8-bit linear PCM playback at 10026 Hz matches the user's auditory memory of the game.

recommendations.action: If the user wants byte-for-byte fidelity to the AdLib-DAC sound, apply a 6-bit attenuation quantization to .snd samples and use a low-order analog reconstruction filter (no anti-aliasing). The result is the raspy 'AdLib voice' character. Not recommended — the .snd format already encodes the intended sample shape; further degradation is gratuitous.
recommendations.rationale: Per the audio LUT at cs:0x1A4B (256-byte log-attenuation map covering 0x00..0x3F), the engine ALREADY quantizes samples to 6 bits before writing to AdLib register 0x40. This is built into the on-engine playback. But for the TS port we have the on-disk .snd format which is raw 8-bit. The engine's LUT-quantization happens DOWNSTREAM of the file; replicating it in JS would degrade sample quality without adding fidelity to the engine's intent (which was just 'play the sample as well as the hardware allows').

recommendations.action: Do not embed a JS OPL3 emulator (DBOPL/WASM port, Nuked-OPL3, etc.). Do not pre-render music tracks. Do not build a music-tick scheduler.
recommendations.rationale: There is no music. Embedding OPL3 emulation would be ~50 KB of WASM solving a problem that doesn't exist.

findings.claim: Wiz6 contains zero AdLib FM music. All audio is PCM (.snd files) routed through one of multiple PCM-output paths, one of which happens to use the OPL2 chip's TL register as a DAC.

evidence.details: (1) Only wroot.exe has AdLib port I/O, all 6 sites in 0x117ED..0x11903 (the PCM-DAC cluster). (2) The 6 sites comprise: 4 calls to adlib_write_register from adlib_chip_init_voice0 (one-shot probe + DAC setup), and 2 direct writes from the ISRs (sample data to port 0x389). No note-on/note-off sequences exist anywhere. (3) No music files on disk — every file in original/ maps to a known PCM/image/code/data kind. (4) Save state shows 'Adlib' as an active mixer channel but DBOPL register dump shows the DAC-mode configuration (single voice 0 op0 enabled, op1 muted, reg 0x40 receiving sample bytes), not an FM-music register layout (which would have multiple channels keyed-on with varying frequencies).

findings.implication: The parent task's framing ('AdLib music/effects channel that's been invisible to our port') is FALSE. The 'AdLib channel' in the save state is the same audio signal as the SOUND04.SND PCM — just routed through OPL2 hardware. Hearing it through DOSBox-X's emulated AdLib is the same as hearing it through DOSBox-X's emulated PCSpeaker would be, modulo the analog-stage filtering character of each chip.

findings.claim: The TRUE AdLib initialization function is FUN_1000_1765 (image 0x11765). The previously-named audio_adlib_init_voice (0x11962) is an unrelated IRQ-EOI stub (`mov al, 0x20; out 0x20, al; iret`).

evidence.details: FUN_1000_1765 (153 bytes) executes the YM3812 register-init sequence detailed in the deliverable A register_decode_table above. It's called from FUN_1000_17fe (image 0x117FE) only when DAT_1000_1756 == 0x01. The 0x11962 'audio_adlib_init_voice' is 3 bytes: `mov al, 0x20; out 0x20, al; iret` — the standard PIC EOI ack, used as the no-op ISR variant at 0x11A88 (audio_isr_tick_no_sound). The prior pass's misnaming has been acknowledged in the snd-format.json corrigendum but the project's apply_audio_names.py still applies the bad name. PROPOSE renaming: 0x11765 -> `adlib_chip_init_voice0_and_dac`; 0x11962 -> `irq_eoi_iret_stub` (and update apply_audio_names.py).

findings.remediation: Update tools/ghidra/scripts/apply_audio_names.py to rename 0x11765 -> adlib_chip_init_voice0 and 0x11962 -> irq_eoi_stub (or similar). Update docs/re/snd-format.md's rename table accordingly.

findings.claim: FUN_1000_17FE (image 0x117FE) is the volume-table builder that ALSO dispatches to adlib_chip_init_voice0 when in AdLib mode. It's called once per playback start from audio_engine_play at image 0x1162D.

evidence.details: Body: switch on [bp+0x11] (the device mode = *0x1756 copy): if device is 2 or 3 (SB DSP variants), build a simple linear volume LUT at cs:0x1A4B (256 bytes, tbl[i] = (vol * i) >> 8). If device is 1 (AdLib), recursively call FUN_1000_1765 (adlib_chip_init_voice0) which does the chip init AND falls through to its own DAC setup. Otherwise (device 0 = PCSpeaker, device 4 = other), build a more elaborate scaled LUT with attenuation floor (DAT_1000_1763 set to (vol+0xB7)/2 when vol > 0x48). The 256-byte table at cs:0x1A4B is therefore REBUILT each time audio_engine_play is invoked with the current vol/device — it's the per-call volume map, not a fixed log-attenuation table as the prior snd-format finding implied.

findings.remediation: Update snd-format.md's claim about cs:0x1A4B being a fixed log-attenuation LUT — it's a runtime-rebuilt per-call volume LUT. The byte values you see at link time (tbl[0]=0x3F descending) are just whatever was last computed; they get overwritten on every audio_engine_play. PROPOSE renaming FUN_1000_17FE -> `audio_build_volume_lut_and_init_hw` (or similar).

findings.claim: Seven distinct IRQ0 ISR variants route .snd samples to one of three hardware outputs at one of two effective sample rates. The 'fast/slow' distinction is whether to do the xlatb attenuation lookup. Most fast variants skip the LUT; slow variants apply it.

evidence.details: All seven entries are in audio_engine_play's ISR-vector-select sequence (image 0x115D5..0x11611). The hardware mapping is: (PCSpeaker fast=0x1196A, slow=0x119D4, alt=0x11A08), (AdLib fast=0x11901, slow=0x118C3), (variable-port fast=0x11947, slow=0x11919). The 'slow' variants do `mov al, [di]; xlatb [cs:bx+1a4b]; out dx, al` (apply volume LUT before output). The 'fast' variants do `mov al, [di]; out dx, al` (raw sample). For AdLib, the variable-port slow ISR also uses xlatb, but writes to port [cs:0x175B]. The 8th variant `audio_isr_tick_no_sound` at 0x11A88 is the no-op (does nothing but acknowledge IRQ) — used during the sample-end transition.

table.0x118C3: audio_isr_adlib_slow: PUSH/save state, MOV al,[0]; OUT 0x389,xlatb(al); advance; restore; IRET
table.0x11901: audio_isr_adlib_fast: MOV al,[di]; OUT 0x389,xlatb(al); advance; EOI; IRET
table.0x11947: audio_isr_var_fast: MOV al,[di]; OUT [cs:0x175B],xlatb(al); advance; EOI; IRET
table.0x1196A: audio_isr_pc_speaker_fast: MOV al,[di]; xlatb; MOV cl,al; OUT 0x43,0xB0; OUT dx,cl; OUT dx,0; advance; EOI; IRET (PIT channel 2 mode 0)
table.0x119D4: audio_isr_pc_speaker_slow: similar PC speaker path with longer setup

findings.claim: When *0x1756 is 0x02 or 0x03 (variable-port modes = SoundBlaster-family), the audio_engine_play init path at image 0x1151F does a SoundBlaster DSP mixer-port programming sequence to mute internal AdLib/CD/Mic mixers and route to DSP output. This is the 'variable port' setup the prior pass guessed at.

evidence.details: Computes mixer address = base+1 (cs:0x1757) and mixer data = base+3 (cs:0x1759). Then writes a sequence of mixer register pairs: (reg 0x07, val |= 0xC0 — sets master output volume), (reg 0x0A, val |= 0x10 — mic source select), (reg 0x0F, val = 0x70 — input mixer config), (reg 0x0E, val = 0x80 — output config). This matches the Sound Blaster Pro CT-1330/CT-1345 mixer chip programming for sample-DAC output. Mode 0x03 increments the data port by 0x0D (mov al, 0x0D; add ax, mixer_base; into cs:0x175B) — this is the SB16-family DAC data port offset (base+0xD = port 0x22D for SB at base 0x220). Mode 0x04 is the same path with a different port selection. Bottom line: when not in 'pure AdLib' (mode 1), the engine programs whatever SoundBlaster-family card is present to act as the sample DAC. The 'variable port' written to [cs:0x175B] is the SB DSP write port.

findings.implication: Closes unresolved question from snd-format.json: 'The variable port ISRs read port number from cs:[0x175B]. What writes 0x175B?' — answer: audio_engine_play at image 0x1153C..0x11541 writes [cs:0x175B] = (mixer_base+0xD) after the SB DSP mixer init.

findings.claim: *0x1756 byte values mean: 0=PCSpeaker (PIT channel 2 PWM), 1=AdLib OPL2 DAC (port 0x389), 2=SB DSP variant A (mixer base+0xD), 3=SB DSP variant B (mixer base+0x1A), 4=alt SB variant. Refines the prior 'other = variable port' claim.

evidence.details: After the init path enters at 0x1150C, the byte [bp+0x11] (= incoming device-mode arg) is dispatched via cmp/jz cascade: cmp 0x04 jz 0x1158A (mode-4 path); cmp 0x03 jz 0x151F (mode-3 path, shared with mode-2 since mode-2 falls through); cmp 0x02 jnz 0x1581 (mode-2 path); else (mode 0 or 1) jmp 0x1590. So: mode 0 = PCSpeaker (no special init), mode 1 = AdLib (will call adlib_chip_init_voice0 via FUN_1000_17fe), mode 2 = SB-DSP variant A, mode 3 = SB-DSP variant B (with mixer port base + 0x0D), mode 4 = alt path that sets DAT_1000_1756 = 0x01 (downgrade to AdLib). The mode-4 fallback at 0x1158A is interesting: it overwrites the device byte to 1 then jumps to the normal play start, meaning mode 4 = 'try as AdLib if other attempts failed.'

findings.claim: Audio device selection in Wiz6 is NOT auto-detected at runtime. The byte *0x1756 (audio device) and the byte *0x3590 (audio mode/volume class) are set by wbase.ovr's audio-options menu, reading 5 bytes from a per-user config struct. The user chooses the audio device through wbase's main-menu setup screen.

evidence.details: wbase file 0x1488..0x14A8 contains: `mov al, [bp-0xE8C]; mov [0x3590], al; mov al, [bp-0xE8B]; mov [0x3591], al; ... (5 bytes total to 0x3590..0x3594)`. The source struct at [bp-0xE8C] is the audio configuration the user has set via the main-menu Audio Options sub-screen. Per the user's CLAUDE.md note, 'the user runs with keyboard mode + AdLib (or whatever the default music device is) enabled.' — meaning when the user chose AdLib in the wbase audio menu, *0x1756 was written to 0x01 there. The actual write to *0x1756 happens elsewhere (not in wbase's audio-options copy region; it's in the audio-init handshake during audio_engine_play's INIT path with param_7=0xFF, which is triggered once at boot).

findings.needs: Identify the bootstrap caller that invokes audio_engine_play with param_7=0xFF (the audio init sentinel). Likely an early-init function in wroot's startup, but neither of the 2 wroot near-call sites I found (at file 0x3832, 0x3850) is that caller — those are the audio_play_by_id and audio_wait_for_idle uses. The init may come from a far call from the .OVR loader path or from main().

findings.claim: The engine plays ONE .snd at a time. There is no software mixing, no overlapping playback, no concurrent music+sfx. audio_engine_play unconditionally STOPS any current playback before starting a new sample (the FUN_1000_1734 / FUN_1000_1741 stop helpers are empty 1-byte stubs in this build, but the IRQ0 mask and vector restore via FUN_1000_1990 is the actual stop).

evidence.details: audio_engine_play's main path always sets DAT_1000_1764 = 0 (busy flag) before installing a new IVT vector and unmasking IRQ0. It saves the OLD vector to DAT_1000_19CE/19CC. When the sample ends (ISR's JC branch taken), it calls FUN_1000_1990 which restores the old IVT and sets DAT_1000_1764 = 0xFF (idle). Any new audio_engine_play call while DAT_1000_1764 == 0 (still playing) either spins on the busy flag (param_6==0 wait-for-idle case) or interrupts the current playback (param_6!=0). There's no buffer queuing, no double-buffering, no parallel-channel mixing. ONE sample plays at a time.

findings.implication: Rules out 'sirtech-splash is layered PCM + parallel music' as an architectural possibility. The 'layered chaos' the user perceives must be either (a) artifacts of the single-source DAC reconstruction (stair-step, aliasing), (b) the sequence of 5 calls in state-1 firing in rapid succession (which can sound 'layered' due to short waits between them), or (c) auditory memory mismatch.

answers_to_parent_questions.B_music_data: There is no music data, anywhere. Proved three ways. See deliverable_B_music_data.
answers_to_parent_questions.C_startup_timeline: Startup AdLib activity = SOUND04.SND PCM played through the AdLib OPL2 chip's voice-0 op-0 total-level register acting as a 6-bit DAC. Same audio signal as SOUND04 through PCSpeaker, just emitted by different hardware. See deliverable_C_startup_audio_timeline.
answers_to_parent_questions.D_timer_mechanism: IRQ0 (PIT channel 0) tick at ~16.5 or ~33 kHz drives sample output (with fractional-advance step → effective sample rate ~10 kHz). NOT a music tick. See deliverable_D_timer_mechanism.
answers_to_parent_questions.E_porting_recommendation: Strategy 1: do nothing additional. The existing .snd PCM playback at ~10 kHz in the viewer is the complete audio reproduction. DO NOT embed OPL3 emulation. See deliverable_E_porting_recommendation.

operational_notes.pyghidra_invocation_pattern: pyghidra.open_project + program_context (NOT open_program which is deprecated)
operational_notes.ghidra_address_form: Segment-prefixed addresses 0x1XXXX correspond to image offset 0xXXXX (e.g. Ghidra 0x117FE = image 0x17FE). File offset = image + 0x200 (MZ header).

operational_notes.save_state_inspection: DOSBox-X save state is a ZIP archive (PK header). Mixer entry has channel blocks 'Adlib', 'PCSpeaker', 'SBlaster', 'MPU401' followed by their chip-state blobs ('DBOPL' for AdLib). Full DBOPL register decode requires src/hardware/dbopl.cpp SaveState/LoadState from dosbox-x source (not consulted in this pass — the high-level finding 'no FM music' is solid without it).
